title: Add cache hit-rate + savings attribution metrics to unit economics semantic layer
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Goal
Add cache metrics into the unit economics semantic layer so Finance/Product/Eng can attribute $/1M output token deltas to cache behavior (prefix/KV hits) and estimate savings from caching.

Context
The internal unit economics dashboard is standardizing blended cost as $/1M output tokens with drilldowns by model/region/tier. Today we can explain cost movement via model/region/tier mix, but we can’t attribute improvements/regressions to caching (prefix cache and KV cache). This is especially important as we tune routing defaults and cache policies (and when cache hit rate changes due to prompt shifts).

Scope (this ticket)
1) Expose cache hit-rate metrics in semantic layer views at the same grain as the daily unit-econ aggregates (day x model x region x customer_tier [+ runtime_config where supported]).
2) Provide an estimated cache savings metric in $ and normalized as $/1M output tokens.
3) Document definitions + caveats (eligibility, missing instrumentation, and interpretation).

Non-goals
- Building per-customer cache metrics (will be restricted anyway; any account-level slices are separate work).
- Implementing new runtime caching features; this is analytics/semantic layer plumbing.
- Perfect “true counterfactual” savings. We only need a stable, defensible estimate that is directionally useful and consistent across slices.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical)
We will report two categories: (A) hit rates and (B) savings.

A) Hit rates
- prefix_cache_hit_rate = prefix_cache_hits / prefix_cache_eligible_requests
  - Eligible request: request where prefix cache lookup was attempted and instrumentation emitted.
  - Hit: request served at least partially from prefix cache (binary) OR bytes/tokens served from prefix cache if available. If only binary is available, we’ll define as request-level hit.
- kv_cache_hit_rate = kv_cache_hit_tokens / kv_cache_eligible_tokens
  - Eligible tokens: tokens that would have required decode/attention compute absent KV cache reuse (as defined by runtime event).
  - Hit tokens: tokens whose KV state was reused (runtime-provided).

Notes:
- Prefix cache hit rate is inherently request-centric; KV cache hit rate is token-centric. This is OK as long as we label clearly.
- If we only have request-level metrics for prefix cache in early partitions, we’ll still publish prefix_cache_hit_rate as request-level and document that it is not directly comparable to kv_cache_hit_rate.

B) Savings (estimated)
- cache_savings_usd = estimated_compute_cost_avoided_usd
- cache_savings_usd_per_1m_output_tokens = (cache_savings_usd / output_tokens) * 1,000,000

Estimation approach (v1)
Use a conservative avoided-cost model using the same compute cost basis already used for blended cost attribution:
- For prefix cache: avoided prefill cost for the cached prefix portion (if cached tokens count available); otherwise approximate using average prefill cost per input token for that slice.
- For KV cache: avoided decode compute for reused tokens (kv_cache_hit_tokens * avg_decode_cost_per_output_token for that slice).

We will implement v1 using slice-level averages derived from the existing cost attribution tables:
- avg_prefill_cost_per_input_token_usd (by day/model/region/tier)
- avg_decode_cost_per_output_token_usd (by day/model/region/tier)

If we don’t have separate prefill/decode costs available at that grain, we’ll approximate with compute_cost_usd / total_tokens and explicitly mark savings as “approximate” in docs. (Follow-up: split prefill/decode in attribution pipeline if needed.)

Semantic layer deliverables
Add the following columns to the canonical unit-econ semantic view (names stable; exact view name below):
- prefix_cache_eligible_requests
- prefix_cache_hit_requests
- prefix_cache_hit_rate
- kv_cache_eligible_tokens
- kv_cache_hit_tokens
- kv_cache_hit_rate
- cache_savings_usd
- cache_savings_usd_per_1m_output_tokens
- cache_savings_notes (optional string flag describing which estimation path was used: e.g., “prefill_decode_split_available” vs “approx_total_token_cost”).

View(s)
- analytics.unit_econ_daily (existing) OR analytics.v_unit_econ_daily (semantic view)
- analytics.v_unit_econ_daily_enriched (if we keep base + enriched split)

Implementation plan
1) Identify upstream cache instrumentation dataset(s)
- Telemetry: runtime emits cache_stats per request (prefix cache lookup attempted/hit; KV cache reused tokens).
- Aggregation: ensure we have daily aggregates keyed by day/model/region/tier and a join key consistent with unit_econ_daily.

2) Add join + computed fields in semantic layer
- LEFT JOIN cache_stats_daily USING (day, model_id, region, customer_tier[, runtime_config])
- Compute rates with safe division:
  - hit_rate = CASE WHEN eligible > 0 THEN hit/eligible ELSE NULL END
- Compute savings per method as described above.

3) Data quality guardrails
- Do not emit zeros when instrumentation missing; prefer NULL with a note so dashboards don’t show artificial drops.
- Add basic constraints in tests:
  - prefix_cache_hit_requests <= prefix_cache_eligible_requests
  - kv_cache_hit_tokens <= kv_cache_eligible_tokens
  - hit rates in [0,1]

4) Backfill
- Backfill last 90 days in the semantic view outputs once upstream aggregates are available.
- Validate that introducing the join does not change existing blended_cost outputs (should be additive columns only).

5) Dashboard integration (out of scope but coordinate)
- Provide column names + definitions to Console team so the “drivers” view can show cache hit impact.

Open questions
- runtime_config dimension: do we support slicing by runtime_config for cache metrics in MVP? If cardinality is too high, we may only publish cache metrics at (day/model/region/tier) and keep runtime_config NULL/rolled-up. Need Thomas Baird sign-off on constraints.
- Prefix cache measurement: do we have token-level cached prefix count everywhere? If not, we ship request-level hit rate + approximate savings based on average prefix length distribution.

Acceptance criteria
- Semantic view exposes hit-rate + savings fields with stable names and documentation.
- Unit tests / data quality checks added for basic invariants.
- Backfill completed for 90 days (or documented gaps) and validated on at least 2 regions (us-east, eu-west) and 2 customer tiers (self_serve, dedicated).
- Dashboard query consumers (ENG-2915/ENG-2916) can fetch these fields without materially increasing query latency (no unbounded joins; pre-aggregated daily table required).

References
- PRD: Internal unit economics dashboard (Confluence)
- Related tickets: ENG-2910 (daily blended unit econ dataset), ENG-2914 (reconciliation), ENG-2919 (cardinality/query performance)
acceptance_criteria: Add cache columns (eligible/hits/rates + savings $ and $/1M output tokens) to the unit economics semantic layer view(s) with stable names.
Hit-rate computations use safe division; missing instrumentation yields NULL (not 0) and is documented.
Add data tests/invariants: hits <= eligible; hit rates bounded in [0,1].
Backfill 90 days (or document exceptions) and validate spot checks for us-east/eu-west and self_serve/dedicated slices.
No changes to existing blended cost outputs (additive-only); join does not introduce duplicate rows at the published grain.
Provide a short definitions block suitable for the dashboard tooltip/docs.
